summary: Runtime version convergence for the CLI. A CLI Run may start only when the managed deployment record, the data domain, the startup artifact identity and the restart barriers, read at start time under the existing deployment state lease, say the process is on the deployed generation. A refused start exits 75 (cli_deployment_admission_refused) and is reported as not started; the operator's interactive draft or one-shot input is kept in a private file and is never replayed. Lock-backed CLI process identity and the runtime convergence strip are read-only views. Frozen candidate 80e73a27 (base 111b2d9c) was integrated with origin/main 4f115705 by merge commit 3e15ea05 (clean merge, no manual edits, candidate logic unchanged). The first original full R9 on 8effd543a (job-bb78ab9f3df4432daf82) then failed three architecture guards; commit cbc3813e5 breaks the runtime import cycle without behaviour change and commit b9fc51508 re-registers the function-size ledger. The PR #118 manifest docs/governance/submissions/20261124-long-session-lightweight-m1.json is untouched.

components.owning_subsystem: Existing ManagedServiceDeploymentStore in llm_loop.runtime.service_control (authority); CLI entry in llm_loop.cli and Run entry in llm_loop.core.loop (fence callers)
components.disposition: A fence that can only refuse. llm_loop.runtime.cli_admission binds a CLI start to the managed deployment record (deployment_id, generation, data domain, startup artifact identity) and reads the restart barriers under the existing state lease; an unreadable record is a refusal. It also hosts the read-only identity view cli_deployment_identity_view, moved there by commit cbc3813e5 with its body unchanged so that cli_deployment_identity stays a leaf module (R9-P2-06a import-cycle guard). llm_loop.runtime.cli_reentry keeps a refused draft or one-shot input in private files (0700 directory, 0600 file, O_NOFOLLOW, owner and mode checked) and allows at most one re-open per deployment generation against the verified release. In llm_loop.cli a Run start takes the state admission before a session is created or the run lease is acquired; a fixed set of read-only legacy commands bypasses the fence and every other legacy command holds a drain-visible mutation lease. A refusal exits 75 and the runner reports it as not_started. The restart idle probe counts active CLI mutation locks as busy. Wake-grant re-arm now happens after admission and run lease. No service, daemon, registry or verdict engine is added.

components.disposition: Read-only views. cli_deployment_identity captures the loaded package identity (source checkout HEAD and dirty flag, or wheel build identity) and compares it with the desired deployment; admission_verified is always false, and the Store-reading view that uses it lives in cli_admission. cli_processes keeps flock-witnessed records of registered CLI processes and treats a record without a live lock owner as crash residue; readers never kill a process; it imports CliAdmissionBinding for an annotation only. The CLI identity report and service status expose these fields, the coordination board route adds runtime_convergence without port probes, and the sidebar strip subscribes to the shared coordination poller when present and otherwise performs one fetch. Nothing here admits, refuses or restarts anything.

g1.necessity: A CLI Run that starts while the managed deployment is switching generation would execute on a superseded code or data generation and could race the restart drain. Whether a Run may start must follow mechanical facts read at start time: the deployment record (deployment_id, generation), the data domain, the startup artifact identity and the presence of restart barriers, all read under the same state lease that publish and restart acceptance use. Model or operator judgement cannot stand in for those facts, and an unreadable record is a refusal.

g2.authority_owner: Existing ManagedServiceDeploymentStore in llm_loop.runtime.service_control: deployment record, state lease and restart barriers.
g2.non_duplication: No new authority. The fence reads the existing deployment record, lease and barriers and adds only refusal paths plus private per-user runtime files (drafts, mutation locks and process records, 0700 and 0600, flock-witnessed). It does not duplicate Run admission, review admission or the restart gate, and it never widens them.

An interactive draft is restored only into the editor buffer and is submitted only by a new human action; a refused one-shot input is written once to a private file and is never replayed; at most one re-open per deployment generation is attempted against the verified release. The operator can resubmit, discard or stop at any time. There is no automatic retry that could produce a duplicate Run.
